title: THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: This is the strongest opening change of texture after two days weighted toward hidden physical networks and consent-centred systems design. It puts language, law and one irreplaceable human practice at the centre, while keeping the aquifer and the nine-day ruling materially consequential. Illuminara can be decisive by turning use into examinable evidence, but Ilo remains the authority on the living language, the tribunal retains judgment, and the valley retains the right to reject the compromise site.

First complete draft for S1, written to the selector's checks: (1) three independently held uses of the word (seed measure, skiff, name-board) gathered from keepers a day apart who never compared notes; (2) one plausible counterexample kept alive (the Crowe ferry right), reconciled only through the annual log and flagged as a place where the test must be able to fail; (3) a sealed, blind performance test in which LEASE, LEND and GRANT predict different actions on the same three objects; (4) a verdict that belongs to the keepers, not to Ilo, with his refusal or silence recorded as neither assent nor refusal evidence and one unresolved handing back left unsmoothed; (5) separate indispensable decisions by Ilo (speaks to objects only), Tolliver (performs honestly), Calder (writes her own fallback, declines to appeal), the council (names the Dry Shoulder) and the tribunal (rules on practice, not dictionary). Known weaknesses I want the critic to test: the nine-day clock is mentioned but the Day Five to Day Nine sequence is thin; the ruling in scene five states more than it dramatizes; the lease column may be too easy for a hostile reader to dismiss as a strawman; Ilo's untranslated sentence is withheld and may feel like a device.

This is an unusually controlled courtroom story whose emotional and intellectual strengths reinforce each other. Ilo's refusal changes the method rather than merely delaying it; Pell, Wren, Calder, Tolliver, the keepers, the council and the tribunal retain consequential agency; and the unresolved name-board result prevents the experiment from becoming a victory display. The closing movement from one speaker to a first learner is earned and humane. Before final, however, the evidence must do more than confirm the practices from which its protocols were constructed: the revision should create a genuinely discriminating test, connect that result to the exact three-hundred-year-old compact rather than only to modern keeper custom, and make the nine-day logistics explicit enough that the seed and survey evidence cannot look retroactively prepared.

T03 answers all three ranked points of the T02 review. Protected and kept: Ilo's objects-only boundary and untranslated sentence, Calder's agency (now stronger: she writes the lease, picks the case and wins part of it), Maren's honest hands, the sealed envelope, the unresolved call, the Dry Shoulder cost, the final seed exchange, and the R10 format (scene titles without numbers, italic place and time first, one bold-name block per turn, no quotation marks). Known cost: the story grew from 2312 to 2756 words, above the usual 2,500; I cut the long double tally and several descriptions to pay for it, and the critic may judge whether the middle is now too procedural. Possible downside accepted: the third protocol column (GRANT) now plays a smaller role than in T01.

The revision is materially stronger. Its best move is not merely that Calder gets a fair column, but that her chosen paddle case defeats half of Illuminara's prediction and forces a narrower claim. That partial loss makes the method credible and gives Calder, Tolliver and Crowe indispensable agency. The treaty evidence and exact clock now exist on the page rather than in the narrator's confidence. Before final, one legal dependency should be made unambiguous and one inherited line should be reconciled with the corrected lease model.

Final after one peer review of T03 with two bounded points, both absorbed. Protected unchanged: Ilo's objects-only boundary and untranslated sentence, Calder writing the strongest lease and choosing paddle case and judge, the sealed card and the two misses, the three-part ruling, the unresolved call, the Dry Shoulder cost and the closing seed exchange. R10 dialogue format kept (scene titles without numbers, italic place and time first, bold name block per turn, no quotation marks). Length 2753 words by the worker's own count (T03: 2756 by the critic's count; methods differ slightly).

A dying language is kept from becoming one man's prison when Illuminara turns a disputed word into an adversarial test that can fail, accepts the failure, and wins a narrower ruling that saves seven thousand people's water while leaving its speaker free to teach on his own terms.
